target_customer: Consumers who want homemade meals delivered, and home cooks who sell them (more than 12,000 cooks on the waitlist in 2021)
problem: Talented home cooks have no legal, easy way to earn income from their food, and consumers lack affordable homemade meals. Laws vary by state and county.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on meals; Shef handles orders, onboarding, food safety certification and delivery

founders.name: Joey Grassia
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and CEO; no education or employers there.

founders.name: Alvin Salehi
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch (June 2021) and the March 2023 Series B release; background not found in an opened source.

competitors.name: Josephine
competitors.what: Oakland marketplace where home cooks sell meals to neighbors
competitors.traction_then: local to the Bay Area; not stated

technical_complexity.rationale: A food marketplace with ordering and delivery coordination is standard engineering; the hard parts are legal compliance and operations.

defensibility.rationale: Cook onboarding with a 150 step process and legal work in each jurisdiction slow copying, but supply is not exclusive.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied Shef in the sources; Josephine reportedly shut down for legal difficulty (undated) while Shef grew.

market_need_then: California's home cooking law and similar rules opened legal selling (TechCrunch 2021); Shef reported more than 12,000 cooks on its waitlist by June 2021.

branding.domain_note: Company site is shef.com; no purchase story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, about bringing humanity back to mealtime

branding.brand_signature: Homemade meals from local cooks, backed by celebrity investors
branding.community_and_virality: Celebrity investors in seed and Series B (Padma Lakshmi, Katy Perry and others per TechCrunch) generated coverage; Shef was named to Fast Company's innovative companies list (press release title).

brand_strength.rationale: Warm, easy name and celebrity chef and athlete backers drew press, but no evidence of the name itself driving growth.

outcome_analysis: Shef used new home cooking laws to build a marketplace for homemade meals, raising an 8.8 million seed in August 2020, a 20 million Series A led by a16z in June 2021 and a 73.5 million Series B in March 2023, for over 100 million total. It expanded across the US and opened to cooks nationwide in 2023. No shutdown or sale was found, though regulation varies by place.
notes: The Series B closed in 2022 but was announced 1 March 2023; the 73.5M includes 7M venture debt. Seed amount comes from the PR Newswire release seen in search results plus several outlets. Company website returned HTTP 403 so was not read. The Josephine source is from 2015 and the funding and shutdown details come from undated search snippets. The release says total funding exceeds 100M. Founding year is 2018 in the seed press release and 2019 per YC.
